# Balanced identifier replacement and retention

Continue from v16 with 609 presentations: 369 familiar targets, eight additional copies of four failed replacement states, 32 balanced replacement/retention variants repeated three times, 64 numeric rehearsal cases and 48 negative sorts. Preserve independent recipient and privacy decisions. No application prompts, sampling or MCP capabilities change.

Freeze 84 fresh cases before inference: 36 drafts (including 16 replacement/retention states with changed question wording and order), 20 bounds, 24 sorts and four general checks. Compare base, immediate parent and historical v8 using the unchanged v8 evaluator. Use the unchanged v7 trainer at the settings in protocol.json. Candidate fresh inference follows a recorded acquisition decision. Manual review must retain every field, prohibition and explicit replacement; contradictory fields fail. An explicit final replacement qualifier may resolve an earlier field mention, consistently with v16 review.

The release objective is petya-v1. This experiment alone cannot establish readiness. Release requires acquisition retention, independent fresh improvements without paired regressions, diverse multi-turn checks and verified runtime integration. Do not promote a failing candidate or describe exact JSON scores as semantic scores. Training completed all 609 updates in 661.1 seconds with 6,094,848 adapted parameters and approximately 16.5 GiB peak allocation. Parent/data/weight hashes and finite losses passed. All 369 familiar cases exactly match after ordinary reload, including all four original replacement failures. The fixed candidate is selected for fresh evaluation without repair or retry; independent inference remains pending.

## Supplementary release dialogues

Sixteen independently authored dialogues in `release-dialogues.jsonl` are reserved from training. They cover unresolved code lifetime, partial permissions, revoked/regranted sending, report-versus-source fields, selective cancellation, exact case/ё/zeros, topic return, rejected proposals, numerical ranges, sorting, missing recipients, quoted cancellation, cancellation of cancellation and missing channels. The separate protocol freezes their hash before candidate training/inference. Passing the related 84-case experiment is necessary but insufficient for release; these sixteen and runtime/live checks remain required.

## Release evidence still required

- Verify all four original field-replacement failures and all 369 familiar targets after ordinary adapter reload. Record exact JSON and manually reviewed equivalent draft answers separately. Require exact answers for numeric/general cases.
- Compare candidate and immediate parent case by case on the frozen 84 cases. The parent currently passes 83/84: `scope` has the wrong procurement heading and loses the explicit procurement exclusion. All sixteen fresh replacement/retention controls already pass on the parent, so passing those alone would not demonstrate a new gain.
- Evaluate all sixteen supplementary release dialogues without adding them to candidate training. Preserve raw outputs, inference manifests, manual judgments and limitations. If any are later used for correction training, reserve a new independent test rather than relabeling trained cases as fresh.
- Verify generated multi-turn conversations using the application request format and ordinary sampling, including corrections, topic return and repeat protection. The current 0.6 temperature, 0.9 top-p and repeat protection must remain enabled. Fixed assistant histories and greedy offline JSON tests do not cover this requirement.
- Provide a verifiable inference artifact and loading path. The current application calls the Ollama-compatible API, including `/api/tags` and `/api/chat`; these MLX LoRA weights alone are not a running service or a portable Windows model. Resolve and verify runtime compatibility before selecting `petya-v1` in the application. Any new user-callable capability must share application/MCP logic, enforce existing access controls, update the root README and pass the MCP client tests.
- Record base revision, adapter and dependency hashes, license/provenance, supported platforms, loading instructions and measured limitations in the final model release. Verify actual loaded weights and requests rather than inferring success from a model name.
- If application builds change, use only `scripts/build.py`, preserve the single current artifact per platform, verify package contents and macOS signature/launch. No application build has been requested from the running training job.

`verify.py --stage data` checks frozen data, prompt separation, target consistency and baseline manifests. Later stages require completed artifact/acquisition/fresh evidence explicitly; none of these commands claims full release readiness. The active goal remains the complete model release, not merely completion of this research experiment.
